text:
Priya Shah: Hey team, Luxora sent back the vendor security questionnaire. A few items flagged by legal — SOC2 scope clarification, encryption-at-rest proof, and subprocessor list. Can we triage?
Sam Carter: I skimmed it, main asks: confirm SOC2 covers ingestion and storage, KMS key control, and whether logs include PII.
Priya Shah: Exactly. They want a written statement that backups are encrypted and where keys are held. They also asked for data residency — they operate EU-only.
Jordan Lee: I can pull the SOC2 scope doc and the control matrix. Quick Q: are they on hosted API or Dedicated? That affects subprocessors and residency guarantees.
Priya Shah: Luxora is currently on hosted API, trial account. They asked whether we can restrict region to eu-west-1 and whether we persist embeddings outside EU.
Avery Kim: For hosted, we have region routing and can pin to eu-west-1, but embeddings are stored per account in our storage tier in EU for EU customers — need to confirm retention windows. I'll check config.
sec-bot: automated-scan: security-pack v3.2 results attached (no critical findings).
Jordan Lee: Attaching SOC2 summary + control matrix: https://redwood.internal/soc2/summaries/luxora-scope (internal link). Key bits: backups encrypted with AES-256, KMS in our control plane (customer keys require Private).
Priya Shah: Good. Can you also confirm whether backup encryption keys are customer-specific or shared master? Legal specifically asked for customer-specific KMS options.
Avery Kim: For hosted API, we use platform-managed keys by default. Customer-managed keys (CMK) are only available with Private deployments or dedicated KMS integrations on a contract add-on. I'll draft the exact wording.
Sam Carter: Also they asked for subprocessors list and last SOC2 audit date. Jordan, can you provide the subprocessors CSV? I'll send both to Luxora.
Jordan Lee: Subprocessors: cloud-provider-eu, observability-partner, email-delivery. I'll export the current list and include contract links. Audit date: 2025-09-14 (Type II).
Priya Shah: Perfect. Can we have a one-pager that answers: 1) SOC2 scope confirmation, 2) encryption at rest + backups + KMS options, 3) data residency statement, 4) subprocessors, 5) retention windows. I want to send by EOD.
Avery Kim: I'll draft 2 and 3. Quick snippet for 3: "All production data for EU-region accounts is stored in eu-west-1 and replicated only within EU regions; cross-border transfers only occur with explicit contract terms."
Jordan Lee: I'll handle 1 and 4 and attach the SOC2 certificate PDF.
Sam Carter: I'll compile and run through legal checklist, then send to Luxora. Priya, want me to include a short timeline ask (e.g., need signed DPA within 2 weeks)?
Priya Shah: Yes — propose 2 weeks for DPA + KMS decision. Also ask if they require a Private deployment quote.
sec-bot: reminder: DPA template v1.4 located at https://redwood.internal/legal/dpa-v1.4.pdf
Avery Kim: One more engineering note — if they need customer-managed keys without Private, procurement has an add-on for KMS passthrough but it's limited. I'll note options and pricing.
Priya Shah: Thanks all. I'll draft the outbound message after Sam/Law review. If anyone sees blockers, ping me here. :thumbsup:
